Rashi on Pesachim 33a:10:1.hebrew: אין תורמין מן הטמא על הטהור - לכתחלה, שמפסיד את הכהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:10:1.english: One may not separate [teruma] from the impure for the pure - [This applies] ab initio, because he causes a loss to the priest.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:10:2.english: Unwittingly - That he did not know that this untithed produce was ritually impure.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:10:3.hebrew: שהיתה לו שעת הכושר - שנראית כבר לתרומה קודם שנטמא. והא דלעיל בחמץ — שלא היתה לו שעת הכושר לתרום ממנו, דקודם שחל הפסח היה מחובר, והחמיץ במחובר, וכל זמן חיבורו לא היה ראוי לחול שם תרומה עליו, דראשית דגנך כתיב — משנדגן, ודיגון לשון אסיפה והעמדת כרי הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:10:3.english: That it had a period of fitness - For it had already been fit [to be designated] as teruma before it became ritually impure. And that which [was stated] above regarding leaven — that it did not have a period of fitness to separate [teruma] from it — [was a case] where before Passover arrived it was attached [to the ground] and became leavened while attached, and throughout the duration of its attachment it was not eligible for the status of teruma to take effect upon it; for it is written: “The firstfruits of your grain [degancha]” (Deuteronomy 18:4) — [meaning: only] once it has been processed into grain [mishenidgan]; and digun is an expression for gathering and piling [produce into] a grain heap.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:11:1.hebrew: עירין - מלאכים. כלומר: תלמידי חכמים, שהם כמלאכי השרת, אמרי בבית המדרש כמותי, דהא דקתני לעיל "אינה קדושה" — בשהחמיץ במחובר קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:11:1.english: Watchers - Angels. That is to say: Torah scholars, who are like ministering angels, say in the study hall in accordance with my [view], that that which was taught above, "it is not consecrated," was stated [regarding a case] where it became leavened [while still] attached [to the ground].

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:11:2.english: And the sentence by the word of the holy ones - This is a verse in Daniel.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:11:3.english: They instruct - They issue a [halakhic] ruling.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:11:4.english: In accordance with me - [Meaning] like me.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:12:1.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said - He is saying that even when it leavened while detached, it is not consecrated either.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:1:1.english: [One who] acted intentionally - In [deriving] benefit from consecrated property, the unwitting [transgression] of which is me’ilah.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:1:2.hebrew: ר' אומר במיתה - כדמפרש: גמר "חטא" "חטא", הנאת קדש מאכילת תרומה. כתיב הכא: "וחטאה בשגגה", וכתיב בתרומה: "לא ישאו עליו חטא ומתו בו וגו'" (ויקרא כ״ב:ט׳):
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:1:2.english: Rabbi says: [He is liable] to death - As [the Gemara] explains: He derives [by a verbal analogy of] "sin" [from] "sin" — [deriving the law of] benefit from consecrated property from [the law of] eating *terumah*. It is written here: "and sins through error" [Leviticus 5:15], and it is written regarding *terumah*: "Lest they bear sin for it, and die due to it, etc." (Leviticus 22:9).

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:1:3.hebrew: וחכ"א באזהרה - רבנן נמי אית להו גזירה שוה דרבי, דהא עיקר מילתא דמעילה בהא גזירה שוה גמרי בפרק חמישי דמעילה (דף יח:) בברייתא גבי פגם ונהנה, ובדבר שפגם נהנה, ובתלוש מן הקרקע, ובשליח שעשה שליחותו — כל הני מתרומה גמרי בה. ואזהרה נמי מתרומה גמרי: מה אכילת תרומה הזהיר — דכתיב: "לא יאכל קודש" — אף הנאת הקדש דמעילה הזהיר. ומיהו מיתה לא גמרינן מינה, כדמפרשי רבנן טעמייהו בסנהדרין, דמיעט רחמנא בתרומה "ומתו בו", והאי "בו" מיעוטא: בו, ולא במעילה. וכן עיקר:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:1:3.english: And the Rabbis say: [He violates] a warning - The Rabbis also accept Rabbi’s verbal analogy, for the fundamental laws of me’ilah they derive through this verbal analogy in the fifth chapter of Me’ilah (daf 18b) in a baraita regarding [one who] caused damage and derived benefit, and regarding an item where [by] causing damage he derived benefit, and regarding [property] detached from the ground, and regarding an agent who carried out his agency — all these they derive regarding it from terumah. And a warning [prohibition] as well they derive from terumah: just as regarding the eating of terumah [the Torah] issued a warning — as it is written: “There shall no non-priest eat of the holy thing” — so too regarding deriving benefit from consecrated property in me’ilah it issued a warning. However, death [at the hand of Heaven] we do not derive from it, as the Rabbis explain their reasoning in Sanhedrin [83a], that the Merciful One restricted [death] in [the case of] terumah: “and die therein” — and this [word] “therein” is an exclusion: in its case [terumah], but not in [the case of] me’ilah. And this is primary.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:2:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi - This is our reading.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:3:1.hebrew: ומינה - היינו נרגא. כלומר: וכיון דמיתה מהכא נפקא לן, על כרחיך הכי תילף: ומינה, מה תרומה — מיתה הכתובה בה אאכילה כתובה, דהוא כזית — אף מעילה, אין מיתה עד דאיכא כזית. וליכא למימר דתנא הכי: "תאמר במעילה שחייב בה מיתה בפחות מכזית":
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:3:1.english: And from it - This is the "axe" [i.e., the refutation]. That is to say: since [liability to] death is derived for us from here, perforce you must derive [it] thus: "And from it — just as regarding *teruma*, the death [penalty] written concerning it is written concerning eating, which is an olive-bulk, so too regarding *me’ilah*, there is no [liability to] death unless there is an olive-bulk." And it cannot be said that the Tanna [stated] thus: "Shall you say of *me’ilah*, for which one is liable to death for less than an olive-bulk?"

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:4:1.english: And he objected to it - This is our reading.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:4:2.english: And Rav Pappa objected to it - [He objected] to those who threw an ax at it [i.e., Rabba and Rav Sheshet, who had attacked the explanation].

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:4:3.hebrew: ממאי דרבי - בתרומה כרבנן דפליגי אדאבא שאול סבירא ליה, דבעו כזית בתרומה? דילמא כאבא שאול סבירא ליה, ושפיר מצי למילף מינה מיתה במעילה — דהיא בשוה פרוטה — מתרומה, אפילו לפחות מכזית:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:4:3.english: From where [do you know] that Rabbi - [holds] with regard to teruma in accordance with the Rabbis, who disagree with Abba Shaul, that they require an olive-bulk for teruma? Perhaps he holds in accordance with Abba Shaul, and he can well derive from it death for me'ilah — which is [incurred] for the value of a peruta — from teruma, even for less than an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:6:1.hebrew: מר בריה דרבנא אמר - הא מתניתא דלעיל בשיבושא איתני בבי מדרשא, והכי קאמר סיפא: לא, אם אמרת בשאר מצות — שכן לא חייב בהן קרבן בשוגג שאין מתכוין לאותה מלאכה, כשוגג שמתכוין לאותה מלאכה:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:6:1.english: Mar, son of Rabbana, said - This baraita [cited] above was recited with an error in the study hall, and this is what the latter clause is saying: No, if you say with regard to other commandments — for [the Torah] did not obligate a sacrifice in their case for an inadvertent violator who does not intend [to perform] that labor, as [it did for] an inadvertent violator who intends [to perform] that labor.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:6:2.hebrew: שאם נתכוון לחתוך את התלוש - שהוא מתכוין לדבר המותר, וחתך את המחובר — שאפילו בשבת פטור, דמלאכת מחשבת בעינן: שיתכוין לחתיכת מחובר, ומיהו שגג בשבת — שאינו יודע שהוא שבת, או אינו יודע שהמלאכה זו אסורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:6:2.english: That if one intended to cut detached [produce] - That he intends [to do] a permitted thing, and cut attached [produce] — so that even on Shabbat he is exempt, for we require "purposeful work": that he intend the cutting of attached [produce]; and yet he erred regarding Shabbat — that he does not know that it is Shabbat, or does not know that this labor is forbidden.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:6:3.hebrew: תאמר במעילה שאם נתכוון כו' שמעל - כגון היו כאן גיזי חולין וגיזי עולה, ונתכוין ליטול של חולין והלכה ידו על של עולה, ומכיר הוא מי עולה ומי חולין, אלא שנסתכל במקום אחר — דהיינו שאין מתכוין למעשה זה. וחייב מעילה, דוחטאה בשגגה כל דהו כתיב, ולא כתב בה מיעוטא כדכתיב בשבת מלאכת מחשבת, וכתיב בשאר מצות אשר חטא בה — פרט למתעסק. והיינו מתעסק — שמתעסק בדבר אחר ובא זה לידו:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:6:3.english: Shall you say with regard to misuse [of consecrated property] that if one intended, etc., he has misused - For example, where there were non-sacred shearings and burnt-offering shearings here, and he intended to take those of non-sacred [status], but his hand went toward those of the burnt-offering; and he recognizes which is [from the] burnt-offering and which is non-sacred, but he looked elsewhere — which is to say that [this is a case where] one does not intend for this act. And he is liable for misuse [of consecrated property], for "and sin through error" [Leviticus 5:15] is written [broadly to include] any [manner of error], and [the Torah] did not write an exclusion regarding it, as is written regarding Shabbat, "purposeful craft," and as is written regarding the other commandments, "wherein he has sinned" [Leviticus 4:23] — excluding a non-intentional actor [*mit'asek*]. And this is a *mit'asek* — one who occupies himself with another matter, and this came to his hand.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:7:1.hebrew: ר"נ בר יצחק אמר - הא לא הוה ליה למיתני, דהא בשאר מצות נמי, אם היה מתעסק בחתיכה — ואפי' בשל היתר — ועלתה בידו חתיכת איסור, ואע"ג דאין מתכוין לזו, מלאכת מחשבת היא וחייב. אלא הכי קאמר: לא, אם אמרת בשאר מצות, שכן לא חייב בהן שאין מתעסק בדבר היתר ושגג באיסור כיוצא בו, כמתעסק בדבר היתר ועלה בידו איסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:7:1.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said - [The baraita] could not have taught this, for regarding the rest of the mitzvot as well, if one was engaged in cutting — even of a permitted [item] — and the cutting of a forbidden [item] came about by his hand, even though he did not intend for this, it is purposeful work and he is liable. Rather, this is what it is saying: No, if you say with regard to the rest of the mitzvot, where [the Torah] did not hold liable one who was not engaged in a permitted matter and erred regarding a forbidden [matter] of its kind, like one who was engaged in a permitted matter and a forbidden [matter] came about by his hand:

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:7:2.hebrew: שאם נתכוון להגביה את התלוש - דהיינו: אין מתעסק בחתיכה לגמרי, ואפי' בשל היתר, וחתך מחובר — שפטור; ולא עשאו כמתעסק לחתוך תלוש וחתך מחובר:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:7:2.english: That if one intended to lift the detached [produce] - That is: [one who is] not engaged in cutting at all, even of a permitted [item], and cut [something] attached [to the ground] — is exempt; and [the law] did not treat him like one engaged in cutting detached [produce] and cut attached [produce].

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:7:3.hebrew: תאמר במעילה שאם הושיט ידו כו' - ולא היה מתעסק בשום סיכה, ואפילו בשל היתר, וסך ידו בשמן של קודש — שמעל:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:7:3.english: Shall you say with regard to misuse, where if he reached out his hand, etc. - And [here] he was not engaged in any anointing [whatsoever], even of permitted [oil], and [yet] his hand became smeared with consecrated oil — [and] he has committed misuse.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:8:1.hebrew: אמר מר במה דברים אמורים כו' דברי הכל - קאמר, ואפי' למאן דשרי הנאת חמץ בפסח קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:8:1.english: The Master said: In what case is this statement said, etc., everyone agrees - [The baraita] states [“everyone agrees”], and it states [this] even according to the one who permits [deriving] benefit from leavened bread on Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:9:1.hebrew: תתן לו - בתרומה כתיב: ראשית דגנך וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:9:1.english: You shall give to him - It is written regarding teruma: “The first fruits of your grain...” (Deuteronomy 18:4).

Rashi on Pesachim 33a:9:2.hebrew: ולא לאורו - אפי' היא ראויה להסיק, הואיל ואינה ראויה לאכילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 33a:9:2.english: And not to his fire - Even if it is fit for kindling, since it is not fit for eating [it may not be given].

Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:3:1.hebrew: ומינה מה תרומה בכזית - אע"ג דבסוף כל התדיר (זבחים צא:) ובפרק בתרא דמנחות (דף קז.) איכא למ"ד דרבי סבר: "דון מינה ואוקי באתרה" — הכא אין לומר אוקי באתרה: מה מעילה דממון שוה פרוטה, אף מעילה דאכילה כן; דהא אכילה דהקדש מאכילה דתרומה יליף, והיאך יהיה בו מיתה אם לא כשיעור אכילת תרומה? דבשאר נהנה ליכא מיתה אלא אאכילה, אפילו לרבי, דומיא דתרומה. ואם תאמר: אמאי אין מפרש: "לא, אם אמרת בשאר מצות שלא חייב מיתה עד דהוי כזית בכדי אכילת פרס, תאמר במעילה — דאפי' בעינן כזית, הא תנן בפרק הנהנה (מעילה יח:): צירף את המעילה אפי' לזמן מרובה"? וי"ל, דאיכא נמי למיפרך: דנילף מתרומה שלא יצטרף:
Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:3:1.english: "And from it: Just as teruma is with an olive-bulk" - Even though at the end of [the chapter] Kol HaTadir (Zevachim 91b) and in the final chapter of Menachot (107a) there is an authority who holds that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] maintains, "Judge from it, but keep it in its own place," here one cannot say: Keep it in its own place — [namely,] just as monetary misuse requires the value of a peruta, so too misuse through eating [requires] so. For eating of consecrated property is derived from eating of teruma; and how could there be [liability to] death for it if not according to the measure of eating teruma? For regarding other forms of benefiting [from consecrated property], there is no [liability to] death, but rather only for eating, even according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], similar to teruma. And if you will say: Why does [the Gemara] not explain: "No, if you said regarding the rest of the mitzvot, that one is not liable to death unless there is an olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf [kedei akhilat peras], shall you say regarding misuse [of consecrated property] — where even if we require an olive-bulk, didn't we learn in a mishna in the chapter [entitled] HaNeheneh (Me'ilah 18b): '[If] one combined the misuse, [it combines] even over an extended period of time'"? One can say [in reply] that there is also [the same] refutation to be made: Let us derive from teruma that it does not combine.

Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:3:2.hebrew: אף מעילה בכזית - תימה לר"י: דהכא משמע דמאן דיליף "חטא" "חטא" סבירא ליה דמעילה בכזית כמו תרומה, וכולהו אית להו גזירה שוה — דפרק הנהנה (גם זה שם) יליף מעילה מתרומה למילי טובא, ורבנן לא פליגי ארבי אלא לענין מיתה, משום דכתיב "בו", ולא במעילה. ואם כן, מ"ט דרבנן דלעיל, דאמרי: "לא אמר שוה פרוטה אלא לענין מעילה, אבל בתרומה עד שיהא בו כזית":
Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:3:2.english: "So too, misuse [of consecrated property] is with an olive-bulk" - It is difficult to the Ri: For here it implies that whoever derives [the verbal analogy of] "sin" [from] "sin" maintains that misuse [requires] an olive-bulk, like teruma; and all of them accept [this] verbal analogy — for [in] the chapter [entitled] HaNeheneh (this too is there), [the Gemara] derives misuse from teruma for many matters, and the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] only regarding [the penalty of] death, because it is written: "in it" — and not regarding misuse. And if so, what is the reason of the Rabbis above who say: "They said [the requirement of] the value of a peruta only regarding misuse, but regarding teruma [one is not liable] until there is an olive-bulk in it"?

Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:6:1.hebrew: נתכוין לחתוך את התלוש וחתך את המחובר - ר"ת מפרש: נמצא שהוא מחובר. דאי נתכוון לחתוך תלוש זה וחתך מחובר אחר — מאי איריא נתכוון לתלוש? אפילו נתכוון לחתוך מחובר זה וחתך מחובר אחר פטור, הואיל ולא איתעבידא מחשבתו; דתניא בהדיא בפרק ספק אכל (כריתות כ.): היו לפניו שתי נרות, ונתכוון לכבות את זה וכבה את זה — פטור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:6:1.english: [If] one intended to cut detached [produce] and cut attached [produce] - Rabbeinu Tam explains: [It means that] it turned out to be attached. For if [it meant that] he intended to cut this detached [item] and cut another, attached [item], why specifically [state that] he intended [to cut] detached [produce]? Even if he intended to cut this attached [item] and cut another attached [item], he is exempt, since his intention was not carried out; as it is explicitly taught in a baraita in the chapter [entitled] Safek Akhal (Keritot 20a): If there were two lamps before him, and he intended to extinguish this one and extinguished that one, he is exempt.

Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:9:1.hebrew: תתן לו ולא לאורו - אור"י: דלא איצטריך למידרש מלו אלא לר' יוסי הגלילי, דאית ליה חמץ מותר בהנאה; דלהנך תנאי דאסרי חמץ בהנאה, נפקא לן מונתן לכהן את הקודש — דבר הראוי להיות קודש, או מתתן לחודיה — שאין ליתן אלא מידי דשרי בהנאה לכל הפחות, דשייכא ביה נתינה. ולכך משמע ליה למידרש מתתן לו: דבר הראוי לאכילה, ולא דבר שאין ראוי אלא לאורו — והיינו תרומה טמאה, דלא חזיא אלא לאורו; דאיסור הנאה מתתן נפקא. ואם תאמר: ובעל הגמרא דבעי מנהני מילי — והא הנך תנאי דהך ברייתא, דהפריש חמץ תרומה ד"ה אינה קדושה, כיון דסבירא להו דאסור בהנאה, דבר פשוט הוא דאינו קדוש! ומאי קבעי ליה? יש לומר: דפשיטא ליה לגמרא דלא איצטריך למיתני בברייתא ד"ה אלא לרבי יוסי הגלילי, דמשום דהנך דאסירי בהנאה לא איצטריך למיתני; ולהכי בעי מנהני מילי לרבי יוסי הגלילי. אי נמי: רב נחמן גופיה דמפרש לו ולא לאורו, קאמר מה"מ — לפי שהיה פשוט לו דאליבא דכ"ע קתני הכי; וכה"ג איכא בכמה דוכתי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 33a:9:1.english: “You shall give to him” — and not to his fire - The Ri says that it was necessary to derive [this] from “to him” only according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who holds that leavened bread is permitted for benefit; for according to those tanna’im who forbid leavened bread from benefit, we derive [that it cannot become teruma] from: “And he shall give the holy thing to the priest” (Leviticus 22:14) — [meaning,] an item that is fit to be holy, or from “you shall give” alone — for one may give only an item that is permitted for benefit at the very least, such that [the act of] “giving” applies to it. And therefore, it made sense to him to derive from “you shall give to him”: an item that is fit for eating, and not an item that is fit only for his fire — and that is ritually impure teruma, which is fit only for his fire; for [the exclusion of an item that is] forbidden of benefit is derived from “you shall give.” And if you say: But as for the author of the Gemara who asks, “From where are these matters [derived]?” — behold, those tanna’im of this baraita [who hold that leavened bread is forbidden of benefit], where [it taught], “[If] one separated leavened bread as teruma, everyone agrees that it is not consecrated” — since they hold that it is forbidden of benefit, it is an obvious matter that it is not consecrated! So what is he asking? One can say: It was obvious to the Gemara that there was no need to teach in the baraita “everyone agrees” except for Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, because on account of those who forbid [it] from benefit, it was not necessary to teach [this]; and for this reason he asks: From where are these matters [derived] according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili? Alternatively, Rav Naḥman himself, who explains “to him, and not to his fire,” is the one who said, “From where are these matters [derived]?” — because it was obvious to him that this is taught according to everyone; and there are [instances] like this in several places.
